summary: iter58 PII at-rest encryption + role-based masking validated end-to-end. 32 unit tests (iter55+56+58) green. New E2E suite test_iter58_pii_e2e.py: 10 passed, 2 expected skips. Encrypt-on-write verified directly in MongoDB (enc:: prefix), decrypt-on-read verified for developer/coordinator (plain) and agent/proveedor (masked). Legacy plain docs handled correctly. tracking_number stays searchable. Idempotency confirmed on UPDATE path. Frontend smoke test passed (no UI changes — masking is fully server-side).

minor.issue: Quality endpoint only returns packages with status delivered/failed; iter58 test packages stay 'pending' so the agent/dev quality assertions are skipped. Coverage for masking through this endpoint is exercised indirectly via shared apply_pii_visibility_pkgs helper (unit-tested). Optional: add a fixture that flips a pending package to delivered to harden coverage.

action_items: (Optional, low priority) Extend quality endpoint coverage by flipping a test package to delivered before asserting masking on /api/journeys/{id}/packages-quality.

(Optional) Consider also encrypting recipient_phone via writes coming from POST /api/journeys — current payload schema does not include the field, so it never gets persisted nor encrypted from this endpoint. Webhook/manual upload paths do persist it (covered).
critical_code_review_comments: encrypt_pii fail-open behaviour (returns plain on encrypt failure) is a sensible non-data-loss tradeoff but should be paired with an alert/metric so silent regressions are detectable.
decrypt_pii returns the literal string '[encrypted]' on bad tokens — make sure UI does not show this verbatim to end users; consider localized fallback ('No disponible').

PLAIN_ROLES default for unknown roles is 'plain' (line 131 utils/pii.py). For a defense-in-depth default I'd flip to 'masked' for unknown roles — current behaviour means a future role added without updating the set leaks PII to that role.

POST /api/journeys body in journey_routes.py:223-233 does not propagate recipient_phone from JourneyCreate.packages — phone encryption hook is dead code on this path. Either drop the field from PII_FIELDS_PACKAGES or include it in the doc dict to match the documented scope.

apply_pii_visibility_pkg mutates input dict in place; while convenient, downstream code that retains a reference to the encrypted doc gets unexpectedly overwritten. Document this contract in the docstring or expose a non-mutating variant for caches.
